edition: Discover — 10 November 2026 · Signals and Secret Doors
intro: A Cornish abduction tale, a shipwreck’s combination lock, and a closer look at a strange radio signal. This edition also has two reads on Christian Scripture and tradition, a retro dungeon crawler, and a complete new horror novelette. The Quiet Isle essay is a 2016 fan theory reposted this week, with book spoilers flagged.

items.title: The fairy abduction of Anne Jeffries of St Teath
items.summary: A Cornish servant claimed six small figures took her to a fairy realm and gave her the power to heal. The article traces the story to a letter written about fifty years later and follows how the reported cures led to a witchcraft accusation.
items.why: An old abduction story with the shape of a Why Files case. The delayed witness account, local folklore and official response each tell a different part of it.

items.title: Underkeep is my favorite old-school dungeon crawler since Legend of Grimrock, and yes that includes Queen's Domain
items.summary: Andy Chalk’s early impressions describe a turn-based, grid-based RPG with dungeons that connect vertically as well as horizontally. He compares its Eye of the Beholder feel with modern touches like an automap you can annotate.
items.why: For a retro RPG where getting your bearings is part of the adventure. The turn-based fights let you puzzle out positioning at your own pace.

items.title: ‘Nor Can Foot Feel, Being Shod’: The Theology of Feet
items.summary: A pilgrimage and a Caravaggio painting lead Chad Engelland into a reflection on bodily resurrection. He reads the risen Christ showing his feet in Luke 24 alongside foot-washing and Paul’s image of the Church as one body.
items.why: A close reading that starts with an ordinary physical detail and follows it through several passages. The connection between Christ’s risen body and everyday gestures gives you something concrete to study.

items.title: Paranormal News This Week: AI Ghosts, UAP Research and Haunted Art
items.summary: KASE explains how a ghost-hunting app turns phone sensor readings into generated images, then examines a proposed UAP study that will compare witness accounts with instrument records. The study has funding and a design, with results still to come.
items.why: The part of a paranormal investigation that makes a good rabbit hole is checking what the equipment actually recorded. Here you can see how easily an evocative image can get ahead of the measurement.

items.title: Horse Girls
items.summary: A new novelette from Nightmare’s November issue. Vesper makes gruesome horse paintings inspired by memories of an old friendship. When horses start dying at Saratoga, that past catches up with her. Content notes include violence, blood and discussion of animal harm.
items.why: A complete story for an evening. It takes an everyday fascination and makes it uncanny, with a nod to The Neverending Story that hints at how far it might go.

items.category: A Song of Ice and Fire · fan theory
items.title: Mega-Tinfoil Essay Part 1: The Elder Brother of the Quiet Isle (An Old Post Reposted For Entirely Technical Reasons)
items.summary: A 2016 fan essay reposted on 7 November 2026. It builds a speculative identity for the Elder Brother by comparing descriptions, remembered battles and repeated phrases across the novels. Major book spoilers through A Dance with Dragons.
items.why: A Westeros theory you can test with the books open. Half the fun is deciding which echoes are clues and which ones the author is reading too much into.
items.source: A Song of Ice and Tootles

items.title: 400-year-old padlock code mystery has finally been solved
items.summary: Researchers used CT scans to read the mechanism inside a brass letter lock associated with the wreck of the Ann Francis, lost off Wales in 1583. The article reveals the combination and explains why some of the visible letters are misleading.
items.why: A real-world puzzle box with a satisfying solution. If you’d rather guess how the lock works first, pause before the article gives away the code.

items.title: Announcements: November 8, 2026
items.summary: The opening of this feast-day bulletin pairs the Orthodox tradition of the heavenly hosts with Hebrews 2 and Matthew 25. It also explains the traditional link between the feast’s date and the Eighth Day, and distinguishes veneration from worship.
items.why: Read the opening for the biblical thread behind the angelic imagery. Hebrews 2 makes an especially interesting pairing, moving from angels to Christ’s suffering and the salvation of humanity.

items.title: Eight great new indie horror games for Halloween
items.summary: Keith Stuart picks eight recent indie horror games, including the eerie fairy-tale adventure Allogloom and Tenebris Somnia, which mixes pixel art with live-action footage.
items.why: Two ways to scratch the retro-horror itch here. Allogloom draws on old point-and-click adventures, while Tenebris Somnia brings back the odd texture of 1990s interactive movies.

items.title: From Terabytes to Evidence: The FAST K2-155 Radio Signal Investigation
items.summary: An independent, preliminary reanalysis reconstructs a narrowband feature recorded while FAST was pointed toward K2-155. Its origin remains unresolved, and the original researchers favour interference. The article links the analysis archive and includes a sonification of the measured data.
items.why: A SETI mystery with the numbers on the table. You can hear what the researchers made from the data and follow the receiver comparisons that make this a harder puzzle than a single striking plot.
